overview: White offers the e4 pawn at once. After 2...Nxe4 White plays 3.Bd3 (the Arafat idea) and after ...Nf6 develops with Nf3 or Bg5 for a lead in development. Black can keep the pawn and return it at a convenient time, or decline with ...e6 or ...d6. The line is a trappy surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Gain time with Bd3, Nf3 or Bg5 and Qe2, building a lead in development.
Take the centre with d4 and e4 if Black does not take the pawn.

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...Nxe4 and bring the knight back with ...Nf6, then ...d5 and ...e6.
Return the pawn when needed and trade pieces.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White's d4 pawn and a lead in development against Black's extra pawn.

character.notes: Early pawn offer and fast development; one slip by Black or White can lose quickly.

gambit.notes: After 2...Nxe4 3.Bd3 Nf6 White has no immediate way to regain the pawn.

soundness.notes: White's compensation is considered insufficient against sound play.

structure.notes: The centre opens after ...Nxe4 and White's pieces aim at it.

approach.notes: Strong players do not use it; played for surprise.

level.notes: A dubious line is never a first repertoire choice; needs to know the traps.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e6 or 2...d6 (declined)
sublines_that_differ.how: No material changes hands, so a quiet game with a big White centre.

character.reason: Early gambit with development leads and quick tactics.

gambit.reason: White gives the e4 pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider the compensation insufficient.

structure.reason: The centre opens after ...Nxe4 and play is on open lines.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner; the traps need knowing.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for development, with the queen often active early.
